description: A schism erupts within the European AI Ethics Council as junior researchers and external experts accuse the body of being captured by industry interests and failing to address the systemic risks highlighted by recent incidents. The dissenters publish an alternative risk assessment, gaining traction in academic and policy circles, and prompting calls for a fundamental restructuring of EU oversight institutions.

In response to repeated cyberattacks on public infrastructure and growing regional disparities in AI resilience, a coalition of northern and western EU member states forms a formal aid pact to fund and deploy defensive AI systems in more vulnerable southern and eastern members. The pact includes shared incident response teams and pre-positioned fallback systems, marking a shift from ad hoc solidarity to institutionalised burden-sharing.
